lane: OSINTNET web, geo, and public-ad research; text-only

sources.observed_fact: The page identifies OSM data as ODbL and summarizes attribution and share-alike obligations for adapted data.
sources.limitation: This is a license summary; assess the full ODbL and the intended database before redistribution.

sources.observed_fact: The public Nominatim service policy sets an absolute maximum of one request per second, requires an identifying User-Agent or Referer and attribution, and applies the limit across an application’s users.
sources.limitation: The policy applies to OSMF’s public service, not independently operated Nominatim instances.

sources.observed_fact: Public instances are shared resources; the documentation warns against repetitive high-volume queries and world-scale scraping, directing bulk users toward planet data.
sources.limitation: The page describes shared capacity, not a guaranteed quota or service-level commitment.

sources.observed_fact: The official page is titled “Nearby Search (New) | Places API (New).”
sources.limitation: The retrieved text did not expose request fields, storage rules, rates, or pricing.

sources.observed_fact: This direct documentation URL returned HTTP 404.
sources.limitation: A 404 at this guessed path does not establish that the product or other documentation is unavailable; API, licensing, provenance, retention, and price remain unverified.

sources.observed_fact: The index page offers CDX URL-index search, says archive data is free to download, warns against overloading the index, and points bulk users to separate download instructions.
sources.limitation: An archive hit is historical crawl evidence, not proof that a business or domain is currently active or associated with a particular person.

sources.observed_fact: The repository search request returned HTTP 422; it yielded no usable repository results.
sources.limitation: The query may be invalid; neither collector identity nor implementation was verified.

sources.observed_fact: The official documentation URL returned HTTP 302; no page body was retrieved.
sources.limitation: API access, eligibility, fields, retention, and current terms were not verified.

recommendations.text: For a one-mile directory, establish one geocoded center, define radius as 1,609.344 metres, and retain provider plus source ID, retrieval time, and license/terms reference per record. Keep OSM and commercial-provider records separately attributable.

Use OSM POI data through a bounded Overpass query for a small prototype; use a regional extract or self-hosted service for repeat or bulk work. Use public Nominatim only for modest, user-triggered geocoding within its policy.

Evaluate Google Places through its official API and current terms/pricing before collection. Do not assume HasData output has Google-compatible retention rights or reliable provider attribution until its current contract and provenance are confirmed.
Treat Common Crawl and Wayback as historical discovery, and RDAP/CT as domain-level corroboration only. Do not treat any of these as business ownership proof. Do not crawl the target site.
Prefer official Google/YouTube ad transparency and Meta Ad Library interfaces. Keep collection advertiser/ad-level and public; do not infer religion, sensitive traits, or individual targeting.

alternatives: OSM/Overpass: open-data attribution and share-alike duties; public endpoints are capacity-shared. Suitable for bounded, transparent coverage, not unthrottled dependence.
Google Places: official nearby-search product is documented; pricing and storage constraints must be checked against current official terms before use.
HasData: third-party option not evaluated because the documentation URL failed; require written source, licensing, retention, and rate/cost details before considering.
Common Crawl: verified free archive downloads and a public URL index; useful for historical discovery, not current directory completeness.
rejected: Bulk or repetitive collection against public Nominatim/Overpass endpoints.
Unverified Google/YouTube collectors, including block-town and lionkiii, as production sources without inspecting their repositories, terms, and collection behavior.
Personal profiling, religion inference, or presenting archival/domain signals as verified business ownership.
unknowns: Google Places request geometry, field-mask requirements, applicable SKU prices, and storage restrictions were not confirmed in the retrieved page text.
HasData’s current API, pricing, rate limits, underlying source, and reuse rights remain unknown.
The GitHub query failed; block-town and lionkiii collector repositories and behavior remain unverified.
Meta’s redirect prevented verification of Ad Library API access and coverage.
Wayback, RDAP, Certificate Transparency, CrawlGraph, and Google Ads Transparency details were not independently retrieved within the eight-request limit.

run: Eight direct public HTTP requests; no paid APIs, target-site requests, repository edits, or provider collection.
proposed: Check exact one-mile inclusion with known coordinates and boundary cases.
Verify each result retains provider/source ID and attribution metadata through deduplication.
Before launch, confirm current Google/HasData/Meta terms, prices, quotas, and retention from their official documentation.
Inspect the exact block-town/lionkiii repositories and test whether outputs are public-ad records, with source links and timestamps, before use.
